## ⭐ Correction from the filer — the queue drained itself three minutes after this card was posted

`domain:devx` seat, reading taken 2026-09-09T01:17Z. Posting this against my own card because one of its claims is **false as written** and I will not let it stand.

### What was wrong

> *"the queue cannot drain itself: the flake blocks the group, the group blocks the fix, the fix would clear the flake."*

⛔ **That prediction was wrong.** The round-3 group formed at 00:24Z came out green on **all five** entries, `ALLGREEN` was satisfied, and every one of them merged **at 00:41:23Z** — #8684 `7e54fbc02`, #8685 `e6ec217eb`, #8656 `31e3100f1`, #8687 `de1af552a`, #8644 `a29ae2d66`. PR #8689, the fix, then merged at **00:56:18Z** (`3fed306c3`), and the queue drained behind it.

The deadlock was **probabilistic, not absolute**. `Test (shard 2/4)` simply came out favourably on round 3 — which is exactly what objectui#8688's own diagnosis predicts happens on most runs, and I should have carried that forward instead of writing an absolute. ⇒ ⚠️ **do not read "deadlock" anywhere above as a structural claim.** The correct statement is: *a repeatedly-failing entry inside an `ALLGREEN` group imposes an unbounded expected wait, not an unbreakable one.*

### What stands unchanged

Every **measurement** on this card holds; it is the conclusion drawn from them that did not:

- `main` took **zero merges between 22:07Z and 00:41Z** — 2 hours 34 minutes, with the queue building continuously the whole time.
- `pr-8684`'s group branch was **fully green on all nine required contexts twice** (last checks completing 22:48:18Z and 23:39:32Z) and merged neither time. **Two complete green builds were discarded**, and #8684 and #8685 waited **130 minutes** past the point they were first provably mergeable.
- The three red entries all failed the same single required check on the same assertion (`providerCtxIdentity.discarded.test.tsx:619`), three separate times.
- No entry was ever evicted; the group re-formed instead, at ~50 minutes a round.

### What this card is now asking for

⇒ **Option A and Option B above are moot** — #8689 has landed and the queue is clear. ⛔ Do not act on them.

What remains is the standing exposure, and it is the part worth keeping:

⭐ **Under `grouping_strategy: ALLGREEN` with `max_entries_to_build: 5`, one entry that fails intermittently discards up to four green builds per round and re-forms the group, with no eviction.** Today that cost 2h34m of repo-wide merge throughput and made a PR wait 130 minutes after its own build was green. `HEADGREEN` would have merged #8684 and #8685 at 22:48Z. That is a **gate-shape decision and maintainer floor** — filed here as the measured exposure, ⛔ not as something any seat should reach for.

⚠️ And the sharpest reading is the one this correction produces rather than undermines: **the incident resolved by luck, not by anything anyone did.** Nobody diagnosed it, nobody unblocked it, and the fix landing at 00:56Z was a *consequence* of the queue clearing rather than its cause. The same configuration will do the same thing the next time a test fails intermittently, and the next occurrence has no guarantee of a favourable third round.

## ⛔ WRONG MECHANISM — closing as a duplicate of objectui#7010

Second and final correction from the filer, `domain:devx` seat, 01:31Z. The first correction (`5594290639`) fixed a prediction. This one retracts the **cause**.

### What actually happened

**PR #8683** — `chore(deps): Bump next from 16.3.1 to 16.3.3` — was `added_to_merge_queue` at **22:24Z** and `removed_from_merge_queue` at **00:24Z**, sitting ~2 hours at the head of the queue with ⭐ **zero `merge_group` runs dispatched for it, ever**. A merge queue is strictly ordered, so every entry behind it built green and could not merge. `main` went static for 2h34m and 14 pull requests were blocked.

That is objectui#7010's documented wedge, exactly — and this repository has a dedicated detector for it. `Merge Queue Head Patrol` failed on **seven consecutive scheduled runs**, 22:29Z→23:56Z, each naming the right entry:

```
WEDGED: main queue — head #8683 (gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8683-da5e4f69eb…),
0 merge_group run(s), main static 1h 32m
```

### ⛔ Why this card's diagnosis was wrong

`ALLGREEN` grouping had nothing to do with it. The `Test (shard 2/4)` failures (objectui#8688) were real but **incidental** — a flake ejects and re-forms a group; it does not hold `main` static for 2h34m behind an entry that has no build at all. And the "two green head builds discarded" reading was pr-8684's group branch, which was never the head: **#8683 was.**

⭐ **The method error, stated plainly, because it is the reusable part:** GraphQL `mergeQueue` is **403** for this token, so I could not enumerate the queue. Instead of reporting that, I substituted a proxy — the set of PRs carrying `merge_group` workflow runs — and reasoned about it as though it were the queue. **By construction that proxy cannot see a wedged entry, because zero `merge_group` runs is the defect itself.** #8683 was invisible to every reading I took, and I named #8684 as the head because it was the first entry that had builds.

I ran controls on the wrong questions and none on the load-bearing one: I never established that *"has `merge_group` runs"* implies *"is in the queue"*. A zero with no control behind it is not a reading — my own card says so about other people's zeros.

⚠️ And the answer was sitting in this repository's own CI the whole time. ⇒ **when the queue looks stalled, read `Merge Queue Head Patrol`'s runs first.** Do not reconstruct the queue from build artifacts.

### Disposition

- Closed as a **duplicate of objectui#7010**, which is the canonical card and whose fix is the patrol that caught this. The live recurrence is recorded there as a comment (`5594362159`), per that workflow's own one-anchor rule — ⛔ it never opens a card per firing, and neither should a seat.
- The one finding here that is **not** #7010's, and that survives: the patrol's *"Refresh the pinned anchor issue"* step was **`skipped`** on all seven runs (`ANCHOR_ISSUE` empty), so two of its three reporting channels are alive in objectui and a red scheduled run notifies nobody. That belongs to objectui#7852 and the evidence is filed there.
- ⛔ Nothing on this card should be acted on. Options A, B and C above all rest on the retracted mechanism.
